StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Single, and the sim leaves Power.on_stack alone, so both sides add on re-application -- PowerCmd.ModifyAmount:236 has no StackType branch and Single only means 'Amount is hidden' (PowerStackType.cs:10-13). Correct, unlike the 15 units that override on_stack to a no-op citing the same StackType (py audit/tools/power_census.py stack). Inert either way: nothing reads Diamond Diadem's Amount on either side -- it is a flat halving that lasts one enemy turn -- and the sole ported applier (relics/diamond_diadem.py:37) applies 1 once per qualifying turn end, removing it before the next application.

ModifyDamageMultiplicative.rationale: 0.5 for powered attacks against the owner, 1 otherwise. Both C# guards are present, one structurally: target != base.Owner (DiamondDiademPower.cs:23-26 vs powers.py:3392-3393) and !props.IsPoweredAttack() (:27-30), which the sim's power now self-gates via `is_powered_attack(props)` (powers.py:3394-3395) -- REVISED 2026-08-04: the old rationale ('the sim gets from DamageCmd.deal gating the multiplier families on is_powered_attack, cmds.py:56-58') is now stale in TWO ways, not just line numbers. `DamageCmd.deal` (cmds.py:332-336) no longer centrally gates the multiplier chain on is_powered_attack at all -- per its own comment (cmds.py:326-331), `Hook.cs:2515-2538` has no props gate and leaves IsPoweredAttack to each implementation, because some listeners (Vambrace, Pael's Legion, Unmovable) deliberately do NOT gate on Unpowered. This power's own comment (powers.py:3387-3391) confirms it moved the gate into itself for exactly this reason (damage_pipeline/G3). Verdict unchanged -- the power still self-gates correctly -- but the mechanism description and citation were both wrong. 0.5 is dyadic, so this power does not widen hook_dispatch's G9 (executed: py audit/tools/power_census.py multipliers, which lists it among the safe factors).

AfterSideTurnEnd.rationale: CORRECT SLOT. Like NoBlockPower, DiamondDiademPower.cs:34-40 has no participants filter -- it Removes whenever side == CombatSide.Enemy -- so the sim's side-scoped on_enemy_side_end (combat.py:792, the Hook.AfterTurnEnd(Enemy) slot at CombatManager.cs:1256) is exactly right and there is no per-creature question to lose. Remove, not Decrement, on both sides. The sim's _expire (powers.py:189-195) pops the power and unregisters it; C#'s PowerCmd.Remove (PowerCmd.cs:287-295) additionally fires power.AfterRemoved, which this power does not implement. Observationally identical, same treatment as the _expire entries in audit/records/power/duplication.json and audit/records/power/flame_barrier.json per binding rule 3.

guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the applier relic now has the combat-boundary reset. `DiamondDiadem.reset_for_combat` (relics/diamond_diadem.py:28-33) zeroes `cards_played_this_turn`, and `Relic.attach` calls it whenever the relic meets a new CombatState (relics/base.py:192-195) -- the sim's single expression of DiamondDiadem.AfterCombatEnd (:78-84). So a combat that ends inside `play_card`, never reaching `on_player_turn_end`, no longer carries a stale count into the next fight, and turn 1 of that fight grants the power again. VERIFIED 2026-07-27 by reading relics/diamond_diadem.py and relics/base.py:177-195. The blocked-on-relic-tier marker is discharged.
